sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A circumboreal carnivorous plant of acidic bogs and fens. Its rosette is usually 2–10 cm across, sometimes 15 cm; a 5–35 cm flowering stalk raises flowers above the leaves.

sections.title: Leaves and prey capture
sections.text: The rounded leaves, about 5–12 mm wide, are covered with sticky tentacles that catch and digest small animals. It resembles Drosera capillaris, a more southerly species whose rosette is often larger.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use is documented in the sources consulted.
